hypothesis: Width replication on data_seed 1. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 1, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=128, best-of-3 controls, seeds 22-23, 6000 steps. Prediction: the N=128 force deficit persists at twice the width, so final trained force R2 stays at least 0.04 below the same seed's 6000-step d_model=128 N=64 value from the paired arm proposed this cycle, while accel_step decodability is unchanged. Values come from probes_final, unrounded. The headline gap uses the best-margin layer, with the layer reported and cross-layer pairs flagged. A layer-1 same-layer gap is also reported wherever both arms list layer 1. Within-run values are read only as same-layer control plus margin, never from the max-over-layers trajectory field. If the paired N=64 run is unavailable, that seed's gap is reported as not computed.
expected_if_true: In both seeds, N=128 trained force R2 sits at least 0.04 below the paired N=64 value, at the best-margin layer and at layer 1 where both are available. The headroom-normalised accel_step margin falls in [0.60, 0.88] and is within 0.05 of N=64. This would replicate f-20261016-012922-fd3b on a second dataset.
expected_if_false: In both seeds the gap is no more than 0.02, at the best-margin layer and at layer 1. That would mean width closes the deficit on data_seed 1 and the data_seed 0 width result does not generalise. A split between seeds, or gaps in (0.02, 0.04), counts as inconclusive.
